content.title: Suspended Disaster Reversal | Lone Mobile Actor, Contact Trigger, Restored World
content.summary: Freeze a coherent disaster field while exactly one adult remains mobile; one small contact triggers exact material reversal and restores the environment.

quick_start.input_format: One readable disaster state precedes the freeze. + Exactly one subject remains mobile. + One small contact point triggers the reversal. + Every displaced element retraces rather than respawns. + The ending proves a restored coherent environment.
quick_start.recommended_input: Establish an adult conservator inside a flooded glass archive as water, pages and shards surge. Let the conservator identify and touch one floating brass catalogue tag. Resolve the archive into dry intact shelves around the same conservator and hold the proof.
required_anchors: One readable disaster state precedes the freeze.
Every displaced element retraces rather than respawns.
The ending proves a restored coherent environment.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Freeze a coherent disaster field while exactly one adult remains mobile; one small contact triggers exact material reversal and restores the environment.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
